title: Old-time music versus the origins of jazz
summary: His father's generation played quadrilles, waltzes and dance books, not jazz; he credits Bolden and untrained routine players with starting jazz amid fast city life.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: How did your father play and those fellows you played with, what style did they play?

Well, they played at old time. You see, those days they had music that mostly looked like manuscript, but they called it German music, you know. They used to come from the old country, you know. Mm-hmm. And that's what they played. And they had a set of books they called Manhattan books, dance books, you know. Well, they had quadrilles and they had mazookas and they had waltzes and they had lances and baratas and all that type of music they played those days, you see. Well, they didn't play no jazz, you know what I mean. Now, old Mamanetta, he was a fine, oh, ace trumpet player, but no jazz, you know. Strictly music, strictly music, and so on. And that's what they played, see. But this jazz business, I didn't start to play in that until I got mixed up with punk and the jazz, you know, and playing around them places. And that come in right after bowling, you see. And the Imperial Band, Perez and those fellas, they started playing. Well, that's why jazz came in. And then all those other boys, these white boys, like Sharky and Rennie, well, they come after that. Well, they picked up right from that and just went right along with it, you see.
Who do you think was the first band to ever play any jazz or whatever?

Well, I attribute it to bowling, you know. The simple fact, the way that thing come about, you see, bowling was a fellow, he didn't know the big as his house, you understand what I mean. And whatever they played, they caught or made up, you see. They made their own music, and they played it their own way, you understand. So that's where jazz started, you understand. Just through the feeling of the man, you understand. He's in provision, you see. And then the surroundings, because the surroundings at that time was mostly people of, or you might say, of a fast type, you know, exciting, you understand. And there's old blues and all that stuff, you know, that came in there, you see. And eventually the jazz business started to go on, you see. But the old time musicians, they didn't play nothing but music, you know.

By the way, I'm about to explain to you. We have a paper, you know, that we'll sign and you sign. And you can put any restrictions on it. Yeah. If you want to say anything, you know, and hold it back.
That's detrimental to anybody, you know what I mean.
Yeah, you can hold it back for 10 years or 20 years or. No need to knock anybody.
No, no. But that's facts when I'm, you see, that's authentic. What I'm telling you, I can back that up because.

Now, you take a lot of those fellas, they were routine players. And that's where jazz came from, you understand. That's where jazz came from, from the routine men, you understand. The men that didn't know nothing about music. They just made up their own ideas. They didn't know nothing about phrasing, nothing in music. No thoughts at all about music. Just go ahead and play, that's all, you understand. That's how jazz came about.
And they were mixed up with this fast life, huh?

Oh yeah, those days, man, things was wide open. The New Orleans was, they had hunky-tunks, you know, you understand. All that, all the lowest type of, you understand, would be in those places, you know. Rouse the bouts off the river and all that sort of stuff, you know.
